commit 3638182e202c84870a138f671f7bf11aabb86515
Author: ot908182 <ot_vaibhav.jain@mediatek.com>
Date:   Sun Nov 30 11:39:53 2025 +0800

    [ALPS10677622] CVE_Security_Bulletin_2025_wk32_August supplement Patch
    
    [Description]
    Security Vulnerability in PowerVR - GPU DDK - GPU Register value contents leaked from secure workloads to non-secure world
    
    The DDK kernel module, user space libraries and the Firmware module have been updated to introduce protection to prevent this information leak from taking place
    This is achieved through the idling of the GPU and the execution of trusted zeroing workloads between the secure and non-secure workloads
    
    Additional firmware configuration is required in the rogue_km DDK build requiring the build option RGX_PREMAP_FW_HEAPS=1 to also be set after the patch has been applied to the DDK source
    
    Limited performance impact when transitioning from secure to non-secure GPU workloads (mainly due to idling of the GPU). No functional impact.
    PSP-19_CL6670160_CL6672631_CL6845128.Android
    
    [Test]
    Boot pass, Sanity pass, xts pass
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: 22d0d6514e28a0d77eaf534b386640176c2f1156

commit 5a02f455c78061cedf9ac6ed2f68628d5f593745
Author: Altria Lai <altria.lai@mediatek.com>
Date:   Tue May 27 09:21:22 2025 +0800

    [ALPS09988507] [c8150] CSF OOM handling in new kthread
    
    [Description]
    
    Under high CPU utiliSation from multiple user-space tasks, the
    oom_event_worker, which is enqueued on a generic kworker thread,
    may remain in a runnable state but experience significant scheduling
    latency, causing frame rendering deadlines to be missed and
    resulting in visible frame drops.
    
    To eliminate latency induced by the CFS-scheduled kworker context, OOM
    event handling has been offloaded to a dedicated mali-oom-kthread. This
    avoids scheduler contention under load, ensuring deterministic execution
    and preventing GPU frame drops.
    
    [Test]
    build pass, whitebox, tuota stress, performance test
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: f8c067d336dca501bb45a7dc51d7088e3bc98622
    
    CR-Id: ALPS09988507
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver
    Change-Id: I383b4c5b37f072d0524193ccdf6778b4c0cd1ebd

commit c2a97ca890904c12731a5f271c2df0d5ba518c15
Author: Garfield.Lin <garfield.lin@mediatek.com>
Date:   Tue May 27 09:21:13 2025 +0800

    [ALPS10019360] [c8158] Fix residual CSG/CSI requests post-suspension
    
    [Description]
    Arm patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/8158
    Support Ticket: 03503520
    GPUCORE-46662 Fix residual CSG/CSI requests post-suspension
    
    If the host sends a GPU SUSPEND request whilst a CSG/CSI have already
    been requested to start/resume but such requests have not yet been
    handled by the firmware, then the firmware might handle the GPU SUSPEND
    request first.
    
    When this happens, FW would usually successfully suspend the GPU.
    However, on resumption the FW would observe these pending requests and
    could attempt to handle them immediately without the host being aware of
    it. This misalignment could cause faults at a later stage.
    
    This commit updates prepare_all_csg_suspension() to wait for all
    pending requests to be handled before proceeding.
    [Test]
    stress pass
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: 9e89361d32abf21c33db58cde351ba398c180b54
    
    CR-Id: ALPS10019360
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver
    Change-Id: I3309ada888868d5838b6f839b166ccc42328b309

Author: GuanWen Chen <gw.chen@mediatek.com>
Date:   Tue May 27 09:20:48 2025 +0800

    [ALPS09988507] [c8155]Lock page metadata for page migration
    
    [Description]
    Arm Ticket: 03497298
    Arm Patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/8155
    
    [Official] MIDCET-5956 Lock page metadata for page migration
    
    Lock page metadata in all operations where they are accessed,
    covering both PGD and data pages. Previously, there were
    several locations where page metadata were accessed quite
    liberally, opening the door to race conditions and even
    use-after-free scenarios.
    
    Make sure that page metadata are never locked before taking
    higher-level locks like MMU and KCTX region. Page metadata
    can be locked either in isolation or after taking one of the
    higher-level locks.
    
    [Test]
    GPU whitebox
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: 0f89353bd2fa4277ee6f44b6b113f8d635f14a66
    
    CR-Id: ALPS09988507
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver
    Change-Id: I89faff97fd13ae1f560957484d5e4da4a646e5db

Author: Garfield.Lin <garfield.lin@mediatek.com>
Date:   Tue May 20 11:02:47 2025 +0800

    [ALPS10019360] [c8152] unexpected legacy sleep request with SoI Enabled
    
    [Description]
    arm patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/8152
    support ticket: 03504912
    
    A race condition occurs when the firmware triggers two closely SoI events
    before the kbase state machine has fully transitioned into sleep.
    Consequently, the host process receives two idle notifications.
    The previous code logic did not account for this race condition,
    resulting in the second idle notification incorrectly issuing an explicit
    sleep request from kbase side.
    
    Solution is ignore the second idle handler if the
    kbdev->csf.scheduler.gpu_idle_timer_enabled in disable state.
    [Test]
    stress pass
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: 3504c5492322a7b166c68238195400d1fff66058
    
    CR-Id: ALPS10019360
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver

    [ALPS09843144] [c8060] Fix for MCU power state transit issue
    
    [Description]
    ARM Ticket:03505417
    ARM Patch:https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/8086
    
    [PATCH] GPUCORE-46206 Fix for MCU power state transit issue
    Currently, kbase PM aassumes two things:
    - neural-present will be always same to shader-present.
    - base power domain will always transit together with
      shader-core / neural-engine power transit.
    
    Both assumptions are wrong as below:
    - neural-present should be subset of shader-presnet,
      but it doesnt need to be same to shader-present.
    - base power domain has dependency to stack and not
      guaranteed to be turned of when shader-core and
      neural-engine under it gets turned off when other
      base domain has dependency to it.
    
    [Test]
    test feature pass

commit b412035a89015d18e280bdaab8cd5850b9f1eacf
Author: mtk15701 <chien-lun.hsu@mediatek.com>
Date:   Tue Apr 22 09:57:29 2025 +0800

    [ALPS09893606] [c8051] a16w: Fix hwaccess_lock check warnings
    
    [Description]
    ARM ticket: 03503401
    ARM patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/8051/1
    
    GPUCORE-46489 Remove the confusing *_reset_gpu_locked() wrappers
    
    The Kbase driver currently includes *_reset_gpu_locked() functions
    that wrap the corresponding *_reset_gpu() calls. The wrappers perform
    a lock dependency check to ensure the hwaccess lock is held.
    
    However, this setup is confusing and has led to incorrect usage: the
    *_locked() functions have been called in contexts where the hwaccess
    lock is not actually held, triggering unnecessary kernel warnings on
    debug builds—despite there being no functional side effects.
    
    This patch removes the *_reset_gpu_locked() functions. Their primary
    purpose was to act as a maintenance hint indicating that *_reset_gpu()
    may be called with the hwaccess lock held. This information can be
    inferred from the call context and does not require explicit function
    separation.
    
    Simplifying this logic avoids future misuse and reduces noise in
    debug kernel environments, while maintaining clarity for developers
    working on GPU reset paths.
    
    [Test]
    Boot PASS
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: 0b0278632d437c3f57ef6d3fcaa60f3151d665a9
    
    CR-Id: ALPS09893606

Author: mtk15701 <chien-lun.hsu@mediatek.com>

    [ALPS09769931] [c7880] a16w: Fix WARN_ON in MGM lp_size Accounting
    
    [Description]
    ARM ticket: 03502241
    ARM patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/7880
    
    [Official] MIDCET-6063 Fix WARN_ON in MGM lp_size Accounting
    
    This commit addresses two issues:
    
    Sub-page Freeing Group Mismatch:
    When a sub-page is freed to a pool with a different group_id from its
    origin, a mismatch occurs, leading to a warning during MGM free
    operations.
    
    Inconsistent Page Order Conversion:
    The pool may accept pages in either small or large order, but the
    nr_pages parameter is provided in small page units. This commit converts
    the large order accordingly before calculating the pools capacity.
    
    These changes ensure proper accounting and prevent spurious warnings in
    MGM.
    
    Revert WA patch 10001644.
    
    [Test]
    Boot PASS

commit 8e08c4e9dc640db9e09507cbcb1315eb26f5ac19
Author: Garfield.Lin <garfield.lin@mediatek.com>
Date:   Wed Apr 16 10:58:12 2025 +0800

    [ALPS09802077] [c7982] Handle runtime suspend abortion with GLS enabled
    
    [Description]
    arm patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/7982
    
    This commit fixes an issue with the driver attempting to confirm that
    all CSGs have been suspended successfully even in case the suspension
    has to be aborted because the GPU becomes active again. When this
    happens, kbase_csf_scheduler_check_gls_success() returns a failure,
    causing it to initiate a GPU reset.
    
    Additional fixes:
    - Transition the scheduler to SUSPENDED state immediately after
      having successfully suspended all groups if GLS is disabled in order
      to retain existing behaviours. This avoids an issue with
      check_group_sync_update_worker() as it expects the MCU will be halted

commit bc250987103fb825b4e01e88614db354efd5a3ca
Author: Christina Chuang <christina.chuang@mediatek.com>
Date:   Wed Apr 16 10:57:20 2025 +0800

    [ALPS09661002] Fix non-idle CSG not resumed after LRU suspension
    
    [Description]
    Arm ticket: 03499813
    Arm patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/7867
    A group that has been suspended due to the LRU optimisation or otherwise
    preemption might fail to be resumed immediately by a queue kick even
    when it should do so. This could occur if these conditions are
    satisfied:
    - The number of active queue groups is larger than the number of
      available CSG slots.
    - The group becomes idle and is suspended, but before suspension
      completes the group also gets rotate in a scheduler tick to the back
      of the queue.
    - The queue(s) belonging to said group are kicked again before
      suspension finishes, causing the groups run_state to be set to
      KBASE_CSF_GROUP_SUSPENDED post-suspension.
    
    When the queue kick is handled, scheduler observes correctly that the
    group was idle before suspension but because the scan_seq_num is larger
    than num_csg_slots_for_tick: we skip issuing a tock for it. However, the
    scan_seq_num in this case is outdated because it is only updated during
    a scheduler tick/tock.
    
    With this commit, the scheduler now always re-evaluates the groups
    runability by issuing a tock when it detects this race condition.
    
    [Test]
    functionality pass, build pass, reboot pass, monkey test pass, suspend/resume test pass, reboot test pass, whitebox test pass
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: f9da0322ef6e5c2b7596ddc434b2a0709a6ae0ae
    
    CR-Id: ALPS09661002
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK middleware
    Change-Id: Ie95b58bf8224bc2e95f7942b1a0efb4cdef187d6

Author: victor-cl.wu <victor-cl.wu@mediatek.com>
Date:   Tue Mar 25 11:22:32 2025 +0800

    [ALPS09773767] [c7854]r54p1:user IO pages after group fatal error
    
    [Description]
    Arm Ticket: 03499218
    Arm Patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/7854/4
    
    Fix UAF issue of user IO pages after group fatal error
    
    The user IO page mappings were not unmapped properly when a group is
    terminated, which could lead to the pages being accessed after
    termination. With this change, the driver shall remap a groups shared
    page to the dummy page during termination to ensure that accesses to
    it will not cause the application to crash, but also these accesses will
    be rendered harmless.
    
    [Test]
    whitebox test pass

    CVE-2024-12576: PP-171396 GPU DDK - Untrusted app can crash firmware by
    forcing MCU access to non-aligned address
    Resolution: The DDK firmware component has been updated to introduce
    protection to prevent this non-aligned access from taking place.
    
    CVE-2024-12837: PP-171580 : GPU DDK - Exploitable kernel double free on
    apsFenceSyncCheckpoints allocated with arbitrary size
    Resolution: The DDK kernel module has been updated to prevent kernel heap
    corruption under identified scenarios.
    
    PSP-28 : GPU DDK - Potential UAF in RGXCreateFreeList in error path when
    PMR_WriteBytes fails
    Resolution: The DDK kernel module has been updated to address the incorrect
    error handling leading to this use-after-free.
    
    CVE_SecurityBulletin_2025_wk06_February
    CVE-2025-0478: PP-171511 : GPU DDK - PMMETA_PROTECT PMR can be exported as
    dma-buf file / GEM object
    Resolution: The DDK kernel module has been updated to address this improper
    use of GPU system calls to prevent unauthorised access to arbitrary physical
    memory pages.
    
    PP-171570 : GPU DDK - Error path memory leak in PVRSRVDeviceServicesOpen and
    PVRSRVDeviceSyncOpen functions
    Resolution: The DDK kernel module has been updated to address this improper use
    of GPU system calls by freeing all memory allocated in affect system calls
    under the identified scenarios
    
    PSP-34 : GPU DDK - _WrapExtMemReleasePages called twice if _FlushUMVirtualRange
    ails
    Resolution: The DDK kernel module has been updated to prevent kernel heap
    corruption under the identified scenarios.

    [ALPS09711481] [c7647] GPUCORE-45487 Fix lock issue with core_mask
    
    [Description]
    Arm Ticket: 03484831
    Arm Patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/7647
    
    Original bug fix added a write to a HW register without taking the
    hwaccess lock. There are two callers of this function, one already takes
    the lock and one releases it early before the hw write. To prevent a
    deadlock, the release of the lock is now done after the hw register
    write.

    [ALPS09475117] [c7571] Execute high-priority KCPUQ commands in kthread
    
    [Description]
    arm ticket: 03487083
    patch link: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/7571
    
    GPUCORE-45207 Execute high-priority KCPUQ commands in kthread
    
    KCPU queue commands belonging prioritised contexts are currently
    executed by the scheduler kthread. This has both pros and cons:
    - Pros: Avoid race conditions with GPU idle worker where the GPU is set
      to idle only to be woken up immediately.
    - Cons: KCPU command execution can block GPU queue scheduling.
    
    [Test]
    test PASS

commit 2d2befd9ab7ab6680c588e40fc715af9b94ad73f
Author: Garfield.Lin <garfield.lin@mediatek.com>
Date:   Sat Jan 18 23:51:14 2025 +0800

    [ALPS09475117] GPUCORE-45207 enable KCPUQ kthread
    
    [Description]
    
    arm patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/7456
    
    KCPU queue commands belonging prioritised contexts are currently
    executed by the scheduler kthread. This has both pros and cons:
    - Pros: Avoid race conditions with GPU idle worker where the GPU is set
      to idle only to be woken up immediately.
    - Cons: KCPU command execution can block GPU queue scheduling.
     This commit moves KCPU command execution for prioritised contexts to its own dedicated kthread to avoid possible stalls to the main scheduler kthread.
    
    [Test]
    test pass
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: 349e653f4b59023e7670b36b17713a1ad15e40be
    
    CR-Id: ALPS09475117
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver
    Change-Id: I94484786641026eea808f8b16d9256131d4556c4

Author: Christina Chuang <christina.chuang@mediatek.com>
Date:   Thu Dec 12 20:34:25 2024 +0800

    [ALPS08760500] [c7250]Fix stalls for resumed CSG after evicted by LRU
    
    [Description]
    Arm Ticket: 03484513
    Arm Patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/7250
    This commit handled a race condition where a group that has been
    requested to suspend when it was idle became active before the suspension
    completes. When this happens, the groups run_state would be set to
    KBASE_CSF_GROUP_SUSPENDED. Because of this, the scheduler would treat
    the group as though it was suspended because of preemption, and new work
    for said group wouldnt be considered again until the next scheduling
    tick.
    
    [Test]
    Monkey test, suspend/resume test, reboot test, whitebox test, basic sanity test, low power test
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: fdcd02d19fc2343dfc643c1b962575453a7645af
    
    Signed-off-by: Christina Chuang <christina.chuang@mediatek.com>

commit 8edcb8a5064406f51fc54119175267f425755e35
Author: yan-hong.zhang <yan-hong.zhang@mediatek.com>
Date:   Thu Dec 12 20:33:38 2024 +0800

    [ALPS09344987] [c7101] Avoid Fence Signal Timeouts
    
    [Description]
    Arm Ticket: 03480454
    Arm Patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/7101
    
    On unrecoverable errors, csf.lock needs to be acquired before
    switching to UNMAPPED mode to prevent other threads from
    terminating or creating CSGs inside current faulty kctx.
    
    Otherwise, it could lead to two consequences:
    1. CSG could be terminated somewhere else so kbase_event_wakeup can be
    skipped incorrectly inside function kbase_csf_ctx_handle_fault.
    2. User space could create new CSGs while the current kctx still has
    error flag -- KCTX_AS_DISABLED_ON_FAULT.  As a result, underflow could
    happen on scheduler-
    
    [Test]
    GPU Whitebox Test
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: e75f140bb46fcfd11e3d693dc1ea5bf06914eaed
    
    CR-Id: ALPS09344987

commit 859c0162af4219e85c124be696d1c3f10bf60fc3
Author: mtk15701 <chien-lun.hsu@mediatek.com>
Date:   Thu Dec 12 20:28:47 2024 +0800

    [ALPS09153369] [c6936] Fix for cache coherency issue due to 2MB page
    
    [Description]
    ARM ticket: 03477285
    ARM patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/6936/3
    
    GPUCE-148: Potential fix for cache coherency issue due to 2MB page
    
    Phenomenon:
        Polygon list DATA_INVALID_FAULT reported
    
    Analysis:
        A corruption issue on the MTKs Krake platform with IO coherency
        enabled,
        as DDK ended up freeing a GPU allocation with dirty CPU cache lines
        the pages for that allocation got recycled by Kbase for another
        allocation
        (belonging to the same context) without being CPU cache cleaned,
        then the CPU cache evicted to the new usage allocation which
        corruption the content.
    
    Root Cause:
        Kbase didnt do the CPU cache maintenance before recycling the 4K
        page that was sub-allocated from a 2MB page.
    
    [Test]
    GPU_Multimedia_Basic_Sanity PASS
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: f50c20cfd7294b7c4893d7a13221d3f75e580d3b
    
    CR-Id: ALPS09153369
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver
    Change-Id: I058a1f0e7da53b574ed71fb750a7626d0e3a619b

    [ALPS08992332]  Fix handling of always_on power policy
    
    [Description]
    ARM ticket: 03473367
    ARM patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/6731
    
    [GPUCORE-42122] Fix handling of always_on power policy
    
    The missing the handling of "always_on" power policy for System suspend and rmmod scenarios.
    For System suspend, there were kernel warnings and PM state machine
    timeout error (which trigered GPU reset).
    For rmmod also, there were kernel warnings and PM state machine
    timeout error but the re-insmod of mali_kbase also failed.
    MCU disabling and L2 power down was not performed as expected
    on System suspend and rmmod. For always_on policy, the MCU needs to be
    kept on even if not required by Scheduler. But if System suspend or
    unload of Kbase is being done then the whole GPU needs to be turned off.
    [Test]
    fail fast test pass.

    [ALPS08840137] [c6623] Fix GFX Car Chase Unhandled Page fault
    
    [Description]
    ARM ticket: 03455382
    ARM patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/6623/3
    
    [MIDCET-4863] GRAPHICSSW-45971 Sliced sharing of WLS pool for AG.
    
    Workaround for HW bug KRAKEHW-2321.
    
    To avoid concurrent use of the same WLS allocation, ensure that any AG
    pass that uses WLS picks an allocation from a pool of allocations,
    waiting for the previous use of that allocation if necessary.
    
    The pool is allocated once lazily on the device when a tessellation or
    geometry pipeline is created to reduce memory consumption for each
    renderpass.
    
    GRAPHICSSW-45971 WLS model warning fixes
    
    [Test]
    GPU_Multimedia_Basic_Sanity PASS

commit 2d6e8399a0470d73b3b85d0a6456b502f979be81
Author: mtk15701 <chien-lun.hsu@mediatek.com>
Date:   Mon Apr 1 20:30:54 2024 +0800

    [ALPS08801671] [c6532] Fix Unhandled PF: Page allocation failure
    
    [Description]
    ARM ticket: 03463090
    ARM patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/6532/1
    
    [Official] MIDCET-5202: Update GPU PF handler to use 4K pages when
    allocation of 2M pages fails
    
    GPU page fault handler tries to allocate 2MB pages to handle the page
    fault if the number of pages needed to handle the page fault are more
    than equal to 512 and large pages support is enabled.
    
    If the required number of pages (2MB or 4K) cant be allocated then
    the page fault handler treats the page fault as invalid.
    
    It has been seen that the allocation of 2MB pages can fail if the
    physical memory is fragmented. This commit updates the page fault
    handler to fallback to the allocation of 4K pages if the allocation
    of 2MB pages failed. The page fault is still handled either with
    4K pages alone or with 2 MB pages alone.
    
    [Test]
    GPU_Multimedia_Basic_Sanity PASS
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: 9cf950c03bcf44baa8ce2891f75ee292db886dac
    
    CR-Id: ALPS08801671
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver
    Change-Id: If309e064883c7ace370f1048a38893e78a8fbcb4

    [ALPS08771304] [c6511] Fix allocate failed error handling
    
    [Description]
    ARM ticket: 03462268
    ARM patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/6511/1
    
    kbase_alloc_phy_pages_helper() now removes the number of sub-pages
    allocated from "partial" large pages in case of failure. Previously,
    the behavior in case of error recovery was only partially correct:
    it was right to free the pages, in order to make them go back to
    the "partials" they belong to, but the function assumed that they
    would also be decremented from the counter. Instead, this is never
    the case, because the "partials" are already considered as
    "fully allocated" and returning some sub-pages to them doesnt have
    any effect.
    
    This is the official patch.
    Revert c6476/2 and apply c6511/1.
    
    [Test]
    GPU_Multimedia_Basic_Sanity PASS
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: bb558d0dcc87d4f9a4fbe8895d0d0755a48d3fa1
    
    CR-Id: ALPS08771304
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver
    Change-Id: I7b03b2b71387987050ecbb41840d32f60ee0e591

    [ALPS08302020] r48p0: mGMM: Ajust GFP flag for huge page allocation
    
    [Detail]
    In the memory defragmrnted env, allocating high order page would trigger
    reclaim that would impose CPU works hard in the background. The relax
    mode would, by unmasking __GFP_RECLAIM, silently try and return OOM
    immediately. This would not harm, since kbase would try order 0 for real
    fallback allocation after reads OOM returned in previous huge order
    allocation
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: c74f01ded999ffc0fd6209de2dc75e7dece31005
    
    CR-Id: ALPS08302020
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver
    Change-Id: I3f718c0092dafcfd8f19e7dcc57e115809ae7939

    adb shell "echo 0 > /sys/kernel/debug/mali0/force_hard_reset_enable"
    3. Check force hard reset enable
    adb shell "cat /sys/kernel/debug/mali0/force_hard_reset_enable"

commit 290c7c710f8cecd8a12410538edd4bbe1a5cb37b
Author: yan-hong.zhang <yan-hong.zhang@mediatek.com>
Date:   Fri Jan 12 20:51:00 2024 +0800

    [ALPS08352916] [5821/8]Handle race between CQS signal and back
    
    [Detail]
    ARM Ticket: 03441866
    ARM patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/5821/8
    
    Because of back to back GPU idle notifications, a very corner case race
    scenario can arise whereby Kbase would try to put the GPU back to sleep
    state even though it invoked a tick to resume the scheduling after
    detecting that GPU queue was unblocked due to CQS signal.
    As a result, execution of the work submitted for the unblocked GPU queue
    would get delayed.
    
    This commit ensures that GPU wont be put to sleep for the 2nd GPU idle
    notification.
    
    A small change is also made to the "wake-up from sleep on CQS signal"
    test to validate that MCU is put back to sleep after the wake up due to
    CQS signal.
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: d7ce7d2e06c0b3a37d75c2f35148f2f30dfbaae2
    
    CR-Id: ALPS08352916
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver
    Change-Id: If3c04324e3f669223ee34984fc3fcc8536916ba4
    Signed-off-by: yan-hong.zhang <yan-hong.zhang@mediatek.com>

commit 4388283061594eaea273c2ef27bf95b86951c1a1
Author: yan-hong.zhang <yan-hong.zhang@mediatek.com>
Date:   Fri Jan 12 20:50:59 2024 +0800

    [ALPS08352916] [c5778/4] Fix racing issue of the CS_STATUS_WAIT
    
    [Detail]
    ARM Ticket: 03441866
    ARM patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/5778/4
    
    As a part of MCU sleep request handling FW publishes the status of all
    active CSGs/CSIs, which helps Kbase know which GPU queue was stuck on
    SYNC_WAIT and so it can re-evaluate the wait condition on CQS signal
    while MCU is in sleep state.
    
    A race scenario can happen whereby CQS signal takes place whilst the
    MCU sleep request is in flight. In such a case Kbase sometimes ended up
    not detecting that CQS signal unblocked a GPU queue that was stuck on
    SYNC_WAIT. This is because Kbase didnt wait for the completion of MCU
    sleep request before doing a sync update check for all on-slot groups.
    As a result, Scheduling wasnt timely resumed and execution of the work
    submitted for the unblocked GPU queue got delayed.
    
    To handle the race, this commit adds a wait for the completion of
    MCU sleep request before sync update check.
    
    "wake-up from sleep on CQS signal" test has also been updated to
    exercise the problematic race scenario and the updated test can fail
    without the Kbase fix.
    
    note: optimize c5778/1 to reduce wait MCU ready time
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: 6e576e38a87ac0765873d2f056773bcb0278e5de
    
    CR-Id: ALPS08352916
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver
    Change-Id: I8011939cf5dc37f50abf0d4f258d0cb4a3119485
    Signed-off-by: yan-hong.zhang <yan-hong.zhang@mediatek.com>

commit cae2381868de8742827c9905394b2e3da10e3bfb
Author: victor-cl.wu <victor-cl.wu@mediatek.com>
Date:   Fri Jan 12 20:50:59 2024 +0800

    [ALPS08352916] [c5838] Resolve race between FLUSH_PA_RANGE and GPU reset
    
    [Detail]
    1.
    Revert "[ALPS08206883] [c5618/2] Temp WA to avoid timeout for FLUSH_PA_RANGE"
    This reverts commit d882d4ef8dec197bb721d85156b53f0603c970d6.
    Reason for revert: formal patch 8004742
    
    2.
    ARM ticket: 03436546
    ARM patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/5838
    
    GPUCORE-37202 Resolve race between FLUSH_PA_RANGE and GPU reset
    
    The busy wait for cache flush commands also looks at the GPU reset
    completed bit and treats it as a completed command. This avoids
    a race condition: the GPU reset could have caused the loss of the
    cache flush command, that would have never been signalled as
    completed, causing the busy wait to time out and attempt an
    additional GPU reset while one is already in progress.
    
    A defect test has been added to reproduce the race condition.
    It can be triggered from the user space, if one thread continuously
    tries to reset the GPU while another allocates and frees memory
    handles; every release operation causes the teardown of a
    GPU mapping with a FLUSH_PA_RANGE command.
    
    The defect test cannot always guarantee that the race condition
    will be reproduced when the defect is present, but it has a
    fairly high chance of reproducing the problem. If the defect is
    absent, instead, the test should pass reliably all the time.
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: 5d0adec55436bd825ff180ee633a2a438e1acf88
    
    CR-Id: ALPS08352916
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver
    Change-Id: I1297537c41d403368294f428295cefe9f1f29064

commit a1b9be14c3d515e5d0fa9bbb0a1ccd08304dd29d
Author: mtk15701 <chien-lun.hsu@mediatek.com>
Date:   Fri Jan 12 20:50:58 2024 +0800

    [ALPS08352916] [c5908] Fix handling of GPU reset during protected mode
    
    [Detail]
    ARM ticket: 03442851
    ARM patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/5908
    
    MIDCET-4818: Fix handling of GPU reset during protected mode.
    
    GPUCORE-28601 updated the handling of GPU reset during protected mode
    to avoid the loss of work for the normal mode CSGs, which are implicitly
    suspended by the FW before entering protected mode.
    GPUCORE-28601 directly marked the normal mode CSGs as suspended if GPU
    was in protected mode at the time of reset. It assumed that if GPU reset
    is triggered in protected mode then it must have been due to the
    GPU_PROTECTED_FAULT or firmware being unresponsive. It didnt expect GPU
    reset to get triggered without any error/timeout. Also it misassumed
    that firmware would always get unresponsive when a GPU_PROTECTED_FAULT
    happens.
    
    If GPU reset is triggered when GPU is in protected mode and firmware is
    responsive then a race can happen between protected mode exit and actual
    soft reset of the GPU. FW could resume the execution of normal mode CSGs
    after the protected mode exit and before the soft reset of GPU.
    Since normal mode CSGs were directly being marked as suspended, without
    sending a suspend request to FW, stale data could have been restored
    from the suspend buffer when CSGs were resumed after the GPU reset. This
    resulted in incorrect execution which manifested as a fence timeout.
    
    To fix the issue, a ping request would be sent to the FW to force exit
    from the protected mode. If the request completes, then all CSGs would
    be suspended in the regular way. Only if the request timesout the normal
    mode CSGs would be marked as suspended directly.
    
    A test is also added to exercise the race between GPU reset and exit of
    protected with normal on-slot groups present.
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: b6647773b81b090cfc3147e87375228c1aeef248
    
    CR-Id: ALPS08352916
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver
    Change-Id: I82c520178a5452b46dc55b16436b558c48a0e0c7

    [ALPS08278868] [c5778] Fix racing issue of the CS_STATUS_WAIT
    
    [Detail]
    ARM Ticket: 03441866
    ARM patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/5778
    
    MCU updates the CS_STATUS_WAIT registers on entering sleep mode,
    but if a sync object is updated while MCU is on progress of going
    to sleep, the KMD might read stale CS_STATUS_WAIT values. In
    at least one case, this leads to the KMD erroneously skipping
    a scheduler wakeup since no group appears to be waiting for
    the updated sync object.

    [ALPS08279981] [c5752] r44p1:Avoid MCU page fault due to kill
    
    [Detail]
    ARM Ticket: 03432979
    ARM patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/5752
    GPUCORE-39009 FW Page Fault on SIGKILL terminating CSG after MCU sleep
    
    This patch addresses a Page Fault in FW address space from Kbase if a
    SIGKILL is sent while terminating the CSG after an MCU sleep. It
    resolves this by making a PM function wait unkillable.
    
    The commit also adds helper functions to allow the caller to chose
    between killable and unkillable waits. The wait done from the code
    that is executed in ioctl/Userspace context, shall use killable variant
    if it is safe to do so.
    Certain call sites for kbase_csf_scheduler_wait_mcu_active() have been
    updated to use the non-killable wait.
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: 77a3b3f8c9b41ad54978414dabfdaeeaf51248f5

commit 1de67c579c72587f85b78c42f6f96a89791cc1ca
Author: weichuan.lin <weichuan.lin@mediatek.com>
Date:   Fri Jan 12 20:49:24 2024 +0800

    [ALPS08217951] [c5603]Handle SYNC_UPDATE when cleaning up CSG slots
    
    [Detail]
    ARM Ticket: 03430595
    ARM Patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/5603
    
    A racing between SYNC_UPDATE and group suspension was reported in MTK
    platform where SYNC_UPDATE was suspected to get unexpectedly delayed
    whilst the suspension request for the same group has been completed.
    As a result, CSF scheduler removed the group from the resident groups
    and later the delayed SYNC_UPDATE interrupt was ignored. This ended up
    the timeout of a fence in KCPU queue.
    
    This patch does additional check for the CSG_ACK.STATE to process any
    pending SYNC_UPDATEs when suspend request for groups is handled.
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: 10befb79a0ecb3c0a6b15b83cb92c77f325c1449
    
    CR-Id: ALPS08217951
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver
    Change-Id: I46280950f8d30f4ca11ae7adbac402dbbd96f638

    Merge "[ALPS08072316] [c5433]Fix for ringbuffer alloc failure after fatal error" into alps-trunk-u0.basic
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: dfefe7e1be59f8e53aba42dcdbfd29dc5a37d7b8
    Change-Id: I11f5fa6250119a013d8cc243fccf7876fb48df01

commit 5a33ec26de3fdb2d4a7eec1268f22392beec999d
Author: GuanWen Chen <gw.chen@mediatek.com>
Date:   Fri Jan 12 20:46:33 2024 +0800

    [ALPS08072316] [c5433]Fix for ringbuffer alloc failure after fatal error
    
    [Detail]
    ARM Ticket: 03425035
    ARM Patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/5433
    
    When a fatal error occurs for a GPU queue/group, Kbase sends the error
    notification to the Userspace. As a part of error recovery, Userspace
    deletes the existing queues & groups and creates new ones.
    The fatal error is handled in the bottom half and a reference is taken
    on the GPU queue before enqueuing the work item to handle the error.
    SAME_VA zone is used for the GPU queue ringbuffer and the memory for
    ringbuffer remains pinned until the refcount of GPU queue drops to 0.
    If Userspace tries to free the ringbuffer memory whilst it is pinned,
    then only the CPU virtual range is freed but the GPU virtual range
    remains allocated, due to which CPU VA space can go out of sync with
    the GPU VA space.
    
    It could happen that Userspace, after receiving the error notification
    for one of the queues, start the error recovery actions and thereby
    delete the queues whilst the bottom half to handle the fatal error for
    the other queues is still pending/running. This can cause the creation
    of new GPU queues to fail if the same GPU VA value cant be used for
    the new queue as the CPU VA value chosen for it. Due to failure, error
    recovery wont happen and Application would crash.
    
    As a fix, this commit updates the handling of CS_QUEUE_TERMINATE ioctl
    to block the Application thread till the bottom half for handling the
    fatal error or Tiler OoM event is complete.
    
    A Base defect test has also been added to verify the creation of new
    queues do not fail after deleting the existing queues on fatal error.
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: 37fb43edc9ca08319917e0bb9de6add01fc8ea08
    
    CR-Id: ALPS08072316
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver
    Change-Id: I1d5d5e74695452944d055c822c40deadbb4ba970

commit d82f63660924d5d8143ec97b3dd138dc88995d9f

    [ALPS08010099] r44p0: Fix an overrun into the KCPU queue command buffer
    
    [Detail]
    ARM ticket: 03424281
    ARM patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/5161
    
    GPUCORE-37748 Fix an overrun into the KCPU queue command buffer
    
    This patshet fixes an issue where we were not doing proper bounds
    checking on KCPU queue command buffers when dumping fence signal and
    wait operation status. Since the indexing calculation was using an
    unsigned char and an int type to perform the addition, the former was
    being implicitly promoted to an integer, resulting in an index that
    would overflow the array.
    
    In addition, this patchset adds several calls to reduce fence reference
    counts in a balanced fashion, and terminates additional dump buffer
    workers before destroying the queue.
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: 1c70404c7d8c986bc8da0b2902423a271cd10e76
    
    CR-Id: ALPS08010099
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver

commit 9e59844a91d06c00fe0f4413b9b71fc9fe0f32b0
Author: mtk15701 <chien-lun.hsu@mediatek.com>
Date:   Fri Jan 12 20:18:15 2024 +0800

    [ALPS07865741] r38p1: Fix gallery3d Unhandled Page fault issue
    
    [Detail]
    ARM ticket: 3384404
    Change: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/4690
    
    GPUCORE-36251: Make HeapContext GPU VA to be GPU cacheline aligned
    
    Customer reported an issue where an unexpected GPU page fault happened
    due to Tiler trying to access the chunk that was already freed by the
    Userspace. The issue was root caused to cacheline sharing between the
    HeapContexts of 2 Tiler heaps of the same Kbase context.
    
    The page fault occurred for an Application that made use of more than 1
    GPU queue group where one of the group, and its corresponding Tiler heap
    instance, is created and destroyed multiple times over the lifetime of
    Application.
    
    Kbase sub-allocates memory for a HeapContext from a 4KB page that is
    mapped as cached on GPU side, and the memory for HeapContext is zeroed
    on allocation through an uncached CPU mapping.
    Since the size of HeapContext is 32 bytes, 2 HeapContexts (corresponding
    to 2 Tiler heaps of the same context) can end up sharing the same GPU
    cacheline (which is 64 bytes in size).
    
    GPU page fault occurred as FW found a non NULL or stale value for the
    free_list_head pointer in the HeapContext, even though the Heap was
    newly created, and so FW assumed a free chunk is available and passed
    the address of it to the Tiler and didnt raise an OoM event for Host.
    The stale value was found as the zeroing of new HeapContexts memory on
    allocation got lost due to the eviction of cacheline from L2 cache.
    The cacheline became dirty when FW had updated the contents of older
    HeapContext (sharing the cacheline with new HeapContext) on CSG suspend
    operation.
    
    This commit makes the GPU VA of HeapContext to be GPU cacheline aligned
    to avoid cacheline sharing. The alignment would suffice and there is no
    explicit cache flush needed when HeapContext is freed, as whole GPU
    cache would anyways be flushed on Odin & Turse GPUs when the initial
    chunks are freed just before the HeapContext is freed.
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: da4ea786771ccf40c8fa6e76be352c6cd243ee92
    
    CR-Id: ALPS07865741
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver
    Change-Id: I8071af2cc7c4e486ff1056d277a7a4e72e166344
    (cherry picked from commit a30de2fc4b16d5ee690176f6315905326dad37f9)

    [ALPS07829641] GPU: GPUSWERRATA-1485
    
    [Description]
    Aliased BASE_MEM_WRITE_ALLOC_PAGES_HANDLE elements do not get unmapped
    on free, leading to excessive WARN on realloc and potential DoS
    
    [Patch]
    GPUCORE-35611 Unmapping of aliased sink-page memory
    
    Aliased regions containing the BASE_MEM_WRITE_ALLOC_PAGES_HANDLE MMU
    sink-page were not previously being unmapped correctly. In
    particular, the PGD entries for these pages. This change addresses
    that issue. Further, care is taken to ensure the flush_pa_range
    path operates correctly, for applicable GPUs.
    
    Also updated various WARN_ONs to WARN_ONCEs in MMU layer, in places
    where these could potentially occur in large numbers, rapidly -
    thereby helping to reduce the chances of system stress in future,
    as could potentially have been caused by this particular issue.

commit 7203880c5c81a47ec4ab08e561dd48199dd3a634
Author: Qoo Lin <qoo.lin@mediatek.com>
Date:   Fri Jan 12 20:14:27 2024 +0800

    [ALPS07645299] GPU: Security Patch GPUSWERRATA-1475
    
    [PATCH]
    
    This commit fixes a very rare deadlock problem that was reported by the
    Customer where multiple threads (including the GPU reset worker thread)
    got blocked indefinitely in an uninterruptible state due to which no
    further CSG scheduling could be performed and the exit got blocked for
    processes that have created a Kbase context.
    
    The problem happened due to the race between the following 3 threads
    - Thread performing the context termination.
    - Worker thread executing the GPU reset work item.
    - Worker thread executing the work item enqueued from the kick ioctl
      invoked for the GPU queue(s) associated with the dying context.
    
    Context termination thread prevented the GPU reset sequence from getting
    started and it then got blocked waiting for the completion of work item
    enqueued from kick ioctl but that work item couldnt complete as it was
    blocked waiting for the GPU reset to complete.
    
    Similar race can theoretically happen between the group terminate ioctl,
    group specific work item and the GPU reset worker thread.
    
    ARM Ticket: 03386360
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: f814ad2ef9f653b3f2b3f0dadb31d6b20ad8c3fd
    
    GPUCORE-35352: Prevent deadlock due to race between GPU reset and ctx term
    https: //code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/4637
    Signed-off-by: Qoo Lin <qoo.lin@mediatek.com>
    Change-Id: Ib24c47a414730ec5e07a2bd347184e4ecc66c51b
    CR-Id: ALPS07645299
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver

commit 8da86dff82e569f1845dd62270dc61fbd64abece
Author: Qoo Lin <qoo.lin@mediatek.com>
Date:   Fri Jan 12 20:14:23 2024 +0800

    [ALPS07645299] GPU: Security Patch GPUSWERRATA-1474
    
    [PATCH]
    
    The commit 68ac7aad0af8d6b608ce6d691368837596b68a25 added handling for
    the race scenario between the Shrinker callback and the freeing of
    memory by Userspace that was marked as evictable, that was causing
    the kernel panic in the shrinker callback function.
    
    However the commit introduced a very narrow race window due to which
    the similar problem of kernel panic can happen again from the shrinker
    callback function, if the callback gets invoked when cached JIT memory
    is already being freed either in the context termination sequence or to
    free up some space from the CUSTOM_VA zone to map a new allocation.
    
    This commit reverts almost all the extraneous changes made by the
    offending commit, which actually caused the regression. So after this
    commit, Kbase would have the bare minimum changes required to address
    the original race scenario of GPUCORE-34710
    
    ARM Ticket: 03386360
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: f72751da9f759b486dd2d2fa7ce6df6ff06f4255

commit 9862eee9ac8c2475b14d5cdadba7eaadbdc786bd
Author: Qoo Lin <qoo.lin@mediatek.com>
Date:   Fri Jan 12 20:14:22 2024 +0800

    [ALPS07645299] GPU: Security Patch GPUSWERRATA-1452
    
    [PATCH]
    
    Through MEM_FLAGS_CHANGE ioctl Userspace can mark a native allocation as
    evictable so that backing pages for it can be reclaimed by the shrinker
    when system runs low on memory. The ioctl can also be used for the dma
    buf imported memory to update the shareability attribute of its GPU
    mapping.
    
    The former case can be abused to mark an active JIT allocation as
    evictable, due to which the active JIT allocation can be freed via the
    shrinker. This would cause use after free on Kbase side when it handles
    the JIT free softjob or kcpu command for the already freed allocation.
    
    This commit restricts the use of MEM_FLAGS_CHANGE ioctl for JIT
    allocations and for any other allocations that have NO_USER_FREE flag
    set for them. There is no use case to support the ioctl in question for
    such allocations.
    
    ARM Ticket: 03386360
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: 3a256b5172614d9cf2deb3b5facfad1c46d0fa28
    
    GPUCORE-35268: Fix UAF due to use of MEM_FLAGS_CHANGE ioctl for JIT allocs
    https: //code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/4632
    Signed-off-by: Qoo Lin <qoo.lin@mediatek.com>
    Change-Id: I6246611e26fa60f5efb47eec3e8c76b79167922d
    CR-Id: ALPS07645299
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver

commit af9136be48a315b3afb0b5012b93b76c1bee6ecd
Author: mtk15651 <bocheng.chen@mediatek.com>
Date:   Fri Jan 12 20:14:04 2024 +0800

    [ALPS07645299] GPU:Handle race cond between CSG & GLB IDLE IRQs
    
    [Detail]
    ARM Ticket: 00463225
    ARM Patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/4515
    
    GPUCORE-35224
    This commit attempts to fix an issue with the host receiving CSG(s) and
    GLB IDLE IRQs in the right order, but only the GLB IDLE IRQ was
    observed. The CSG IDLE IRQs wouldnt be seen until the IRQ handler is
    invoked again.
    
    The reason for this is that the IRQ handler performs a number of checks:
    1) Check for CSG IRQs
    2) Check for GLB IRQs
    
    If in between steps 1) and 2), the firmware raises SYNC_UPDATE, CSG
    IDLE and GLB IDLE IRQs in quick succession so that the host observes the
    GLB IDLE IRQ in step 2), then the GPU idle worker would be queued.
    
    Once the SYNC_UPDATE IRQ is served, the host would consider that the GPU
    has become active again. The GPU idle worker, once it executes, would
    ignore the GPU idle event, leaving the GPU powered on.
    
    With this commit, the host shall take note of whether the GLB IDLE IRQ
    was handled in the same IRQ handler invocation. If that is the case, it
    would consider the GPU to not have become active again.
    
    - OdroidN2 test failures were reported in GPUSWDEVOP-1409
    - BASE_L64_CSF and Backward compat test failures were also seen on trunk
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: 60a55aa1ec3f8d361fd6ff449012ab7bb5354662
    
    TI2: 904712
    TI2: 904711 (GPU Core CS CSF)
    TI2: 905496 (extra Android tests)
    Type: Fix
    Change-Id: I3c133641cda7b6b7d94afedfeaad43ff4dabb81d
    Signed-off-by: mtk15651 <bocheng.chen@mediatek.com>
    CR-Id: ALPS07645299
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver

commit 7f9c4dec247a8faa3ef19efac5e49ec8d56f096f
Author: mtk16965 <holiday.cheng@mediatek.com>
Date:   Fri Jan 12 20:13:05 2024 +0800

    [ALPS07401415] GPU: PMA allocation recording
    
    [Detail]
    In order to dump the PMA allocation status, we will record the
    PMA allocating each time the allocation requested.
    
    The recording is stored in a array of structure simple_pma_recording.
    The array lenth is equal to the MAX_NUM_ACITVE_CONTEXT
    which is calculated from the following formula.
    (2048 pages (8MB reserved memory) - 64 pages (CSF firmware usage))
    / 7 pages (for each queue group) = 283
    
    Each time the allocation happen, it will be recorded in the structure
    simple_pma_recording according to tgid.
    If the tgid not exist, the empty entry in recording array will be used.
    
    Each time the free happen, the allocation pages will be reduced
    according to tgid.
    If the allocation pages equals to zero, the tgid of entry will be set
    to -1 as the entry is not used.
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: f9fb772111182a5955a3366f3ce3505f3a3fbd3f
    
    CR-Id: ALPS07401415
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver
    Change-Id: I977ac09413f5d1016ad88997edb83d0fe715cac6

    [GPUCORE-35221] Defer the freeing of VA regions in the chunked tiler
                    heap shrinker callback
    
    This patchset removes the dependence on the region lock in the chunked
    tiler heap shrinker callbacks by operating solely on the physical
    backing of allocated regions. This is done by:
    * Not freeing the chunks directly in the tiler shrinker code, and
      instead deferring actual delection to a workqueue.
    * Even so, we ensure the tiler heap chunks have their memory footprint
      almost completely freed by making the tiler shrinker do the following
      instead of deleting them immediately:
      * first removing the GPU mapping
      * freeing the backing of the chunks
    * moving kbase_vmap() calls on the heap context, buffer descriptor, and
      tiler chunks to tiler heap initialization time, as these can also
      allocate memory for the mapping in the kernel and cause the deadlock.
      * For buffer descriptors, these are allowed to be CPU cached and so
        correct sync operations are also inserted around access to the
        buffer descriptors.
      * KBASE_PERMANENTLY_MAPPED_MEM_LIMIT_PAGES has been raised as such
        mappings have been marked as permanent and will be accounted for
        as such and obey the limits. The limit has been increased by >16MiB
        and rounded up to 64MiB (4096 x 2MiB chunk regions would occupy
        8GiB of physical memory, we map in the first page, so 4KiB*4096
        extra permanent mapping is required).
      * Note that kbase_vunmap() has no such restrictions and may be used
        without the reg_lock.
    
    To prevent deadlock in the shrinker operations themselves, the
    kbase_context reg_lock is not held in the shrinker or anywhere else the
    tiler_heaps.lock is held. Iinstead, certain flags and state are set on
    the various memory regions being read and operated upon to allow
    ownership of such regions to be transferred to the tiler heap code and
    shrinker. This also involves ensuring that no other code-path could
    have a valid reference to the underlying physical pages, as they can be
    changed by the tiler heap shrinker without holding the region lock.
    
    Hence, the virtual memory interfaces that rely on this behaviour
    (kbase_vmap, mmap, kbase_mem_alias and others) will now ignore tiler
    heap chunks through a combination of the DONT_NEED and NO_USER_FREE
    flags. The same is done for the tiler buffer descriptor region, to
    ensure there are no race conditions that arise when the memory is being
    moved to the management of the tiler heap. Note that both flags are
    removed before freeing tiler heap chunks on freeing them, so that the
    kbase_mem_free_region() related code does not confuse them with regions
    that are on the JIT/ephemeral shrinker.
    
    We also restructured how new chunk allocation on tiler out-of-memory
    events is handled, to fix the potential deadlock in GPUCORE-35328.  When
    allocating memory while holding the tiler heap lock in low memory
    conditions, it is possible for the kernel to invoke the tiler heap
    shrinker, which needs to take the same tiler heap lock. Hence, we split
    the allocation of the chunk (which does not require the
    tiler_heaps.lock) from the linking in of the chunk (which does require
    that lock) so that the region lock and no memory allocation happens
    under the tiler_heaps.lock during a TILER_OOM event.
    
    To facilitate this:
    * a lot of the existing code in kbase_csf_tiler_heap.c was refactored,
      and is overall functionally equivalent where we were not taking the
      region lock.
    * a new interface kbase_vmap_reg() is introduced to be used when a
      region has already been looked up and is guaranteed to still exist
      since that lookup. This also allows us to mark longer-term mappings
      as effectively permanent mapped, and so respect permanent kernel
      mapping limits.
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: 4b04471e30e48e91c032c74313e32a4cbc9ebf97

    [ALPS07553785] Serialize access to GLB_DB_REQ to ring CSG doorbell
    
    ARM Ticket : 00479758
    patch : 4494
    
    This commit fixes the race between the ring of CSG doorbell to send the
    acknowledgment for the CS_FAULT event and the ring of CSG doorbell for
    sending the CSG start/resume request. Due to the race the update made to
    GLB_DB_REQ for the start/resume request was lost and so the request timed
    out.
    
    The acknowledgment for the CS_FAULT event is sent in interrupt handler
    whereas CSG requests are sent in the process context where Scheduler
    mutex is held. To serialize the access to GLB_DB_REQ between interrupt
    handler and process context, this commit uses the interrupt_lock.
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: f0fc08091ce1bd1808d18cb86e0186598c8bd9c7

Author: mtk15651 <bocheng.chen@mediatek.com>
Date:   Fri Jan 12 20:12:00 2024 +0800

    [ALPS07551168] Order write to JOB_IRQ_CLEAR reg with read from iface mem
    
    [Detail]
    ARM Ticket: 00463225
    ARM Patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/4459
    
    GPUCORE-35070
    MTK reported an issue on Turse platform where sometimes Kbase misses the
    CSG idle event notification from FW. This happens when FW sends back to
    back notifications for the same CSG for events like SYNC_UPDATE and IDLE
    but Kbase gets a single IRQ and observes only the first event.
    
    The issue was root caused to a barrier missing on Kbase side between the
    write to JOB_IRQ_CLEAR register and the read from interface memory, i.e.
    CSG_ACK. Without the barrier there is no guarantee about the ordering,
    the write to JOB_IRQ_CLEAR can take effect after the read from interface
    memory.
    The ordering is needed considering the way FW & Kbase writes to the
    JOB_IRQ_RAWSTAT & JOB_IRQ_CLEAR registers without any synchronization.
    
    This commit adds dmb(osh) barrier after the write to JOB_IRQ_CLEAR to
    resolve the issue.
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: 3b51b9d65a2bd6ec1d9de65b2130bc9030bcb1fe
    
    TI2: 896668 (PLAN-12467r490 TGT CS Nightly, few CSF scenarios)
    CR-Id: ALPS07551168
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK middleware
    Change-Id: I66b4972d8e916134429f238766b0ff88ada156e9
    Signed-off-by: mtk15651 <bocheng.chen@mediatek.com>

commit 9d321ba058a36498141ae881ef137098b0ac61f6
Author: Anita Chen <anita.chen@mediatek.com>
Date:   Fri Jan 12 20:09:58 2024 +0800

    [ALPS07439684] GPU: fix wait_for_scheduler_to_exit_sleep usleep
    
    ARM Ticket: 00462030
    ARM Patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/4284/3
    
    GPUCORE-34793: Force immediate exit from sleep on group termination
    MIDCET-4124 reported a problem that Application thread can get blocked
    for some time when terminating the group and GPU is in sleep state.
    
    If Scheduler is in SLEEPING state when Kbase receives the ioctl to
    terminate the group, it would wait for the Scheduler to exit the
    SLEEPING state instead of waking up the GPU immediately.
    It was assumed that groups termination would usually be done at the
    time of context termination when the Application is closing.
    And so it may not be optimal to take the GPU out of sleep state just
    for the group termination.
    Sleeping state is a transitory state and once the runtime suspend
    callback is invoked, the group would automatically be taken off the
    slot. So even if the Application thread gets stuck for some time, it
    would still be fine as App is anyways getting closed/killed.
    
    But as seen in MIDCET-4124, some Apps can destroy groups at random
    points and not necessarily when App is exiting.
    
    This commit forces Scheduler to immediately exit the sleep state on
    group termination.
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: 1e183f24608bc5dcf5eda2532d70d77acd7b3617
    
    Signed-off-by: Anita Chen <anita.chen@mediatek.com>
    CR-Id: ALPS07439684
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver
    Change-Id: Ib8efb3c3efe2dca69712c5427bc14927da46078b

Author: GuanWen Chen <gw.chen@mediatek.com>

    [ALPS07435341] Avoid mutex not initialize
    
    [Detail]
    ARM Ticket: 00458671
    ARM Patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/4312
    
    GPUCORE-34570 Avoid calling kbase_pm_gpu_sleep_allowed before late-backend init.
    
    However kbase_pm_gpu_sleep_allowed call from firmware init
    should not be called before late backend init as this would lead to
    the kbase_pm_gpu_sleep_allowed would return false and we would end up
    using a higher value for GPU idle hysteresis timer and thus keep
    the GPU active for a longer time.
    
     - Introduce-  csf_late_init for this purpose.
     - Rename firmware_init to load_init
     - firmware_term to firmware_unload_term.
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: 665a47f571b932f82abe5923b769e2ef8956e0ee
    
    Signed-off-by: GuanWen Chen <gw.chen@mediatek.com>

    [ALPS07382267] r38p1: common: fix mutex not init
    
    [Ticket]
    00458671
    
    [Detail]
    The fix introduced in trunk@d7a1c1ca28
    moved the early init before the late backend
    init due to issues reported in GPUCORE-34233
    
    However kbase_pm_gpu_sleep_allowed call
    from firmware init should not be called
    before late backend init as this would lead to
    the kbase_pm_gpu_sleep_allowed would return
    false and we would end up using a higher value
    for GPU idle hysteresis timer and thus keep
    the GPU active for a longer time.
    
     - Introduce-  csf_late_init for this purpose.
     - Rename firmware_init to load_init
     - firmware_term to firmware_unload_term.
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: 0734e9a02c44ade8093bf5b8ae7b54986e2f7030
    
    CR-Id: ALPS07382267
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver
    Change-Id: I03419fd56e35fec24ae9adffe45c88a08782609d

commit e9d9ff71473866fe56567439741abeb1a512eb7c
Author: GuanWen Chen <gw.chen@mediatek.com>
Date:   Fri Jan 12 20:08:07 2024 +0800

    [ALPS07382267] Fix uninitialized Scheduler lock
    
    [Detail]
    ARM ticket: 00458671
    ARM patch: aa68610.diff
    
    [PATCH] GPUCORE-34233: Fix kernel warning issue due to uninitialized Scheduler lock
    
    The commit 13105d8134de3ede59b2a3964a3b8bfd610e0243 introduced a race
    during the insmod of mali_kbase.ko due to which Kbase can try to acquire
    the Scheduler mutex, from the runtime suspend callback function, that
    wasnt explicitly initialized by Kbase (the mutex structure would have
    been zeroed out though).
    On kernels where LOCKDEP is enabled this resulted in a kernel warning,
    but there was no other Customer visible impact of this issue.
    
    The runtime suspend can happen between the call to kbase_pm_context_idle
    and kbase_csf_scheduler_early_init where mutex is initialized.
    
    This commit fixes the issue by reordering the init calls so that
    kbase_csf_early_init() gets invoked before kbase_backend_late_init().
    
    TI2: 860998 (PLAN-11965r689 DDK Precommit)
    TI2: 860984 (PLAN-12467r450 TGT CS Nightly)(BASE_L64_CSF)

commit 65f4bf4ceaf4591d8d78d4c95706ec232391b1fe
Author: GuanWen Chen <gw.chen@mediatek.com>
Date:   Fri Jan 12 20:07:32 2024 +0800

    [ALPS07212592] [r38p1] Wait for cores in case of downscaling (c4198)
    
    [Detail]
    ARM ticket: 00448615
    ARM patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/4198
    
    [PATCH] GPUCORE-34296: Make the wait for downscaling of cores more robust
    
    The commit c8388f826b063659f2e521172ee5d4b073c334e0 added a wait for the
    completion of downscaling of shader cores, so that the voltage can be
    safely lowered.
    
    The wait was done using the function kbase_pm_wait_for_desired_state()
    if MCU was needed & GPU was powered up. The wait was done conditionally
    to avoid the deadlock (or power transition timeout) where the GPU power
    up gets blocked inside the platform specific callback_power_on()
    function due to the thread that called into Kbase (from the platform
    specific code) to perform the downscaling & then ended up waiting for
    the completion of downscale request.
    However the deadlock (or power transition timeout) problem was still
    seen despite the completion of downscale request due to the delayed
    wake up of the thread where by the time the thread woke up a power
    down transition started and on the completion of power down transition
    when the thread was woken up again a power up transition had begun.
    
    A new wait function is added kbase_pm_wait_for_cores_down_scale()
    that would end the wait if MCU is found to be in a stable ON or
    inactive state, as in both cases the cores downscaling would have
    completed effectively.
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: f974a33eac3c4725661fd6d214cdd23b928f48ad
    
    Signed-off-by: GuanWen Chen <gw.chen@mediatek.com>
    CR-Id: ALPS07212592
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver
    Change-Id: Id13ef2356ab38913d2c2cdfa2560f1f11d697302

    [ALPS07344379] [r38p1] Fix race with kctx->csf.event.error_list
    
    [Detail]
    ARM ticket: 00453645
    ARM patch: 7f7250e.diff
    
    [PATCH] GPUCORE-34474 Fix race with kctx->csf.event.error_list
    
    There has been noted that the function:
      kbase_csf_queue_group_terminate()
    has race condition with regard to the terminating CSGs queued events.
    
    This commit places the events flushing of the given terminating CSG
    before the clean up actions that includes the removal of the error
    events from the kctx maintained list. This rejigged order of execution
    avoids the noted race, which can lead to some access after free
    situation.

                 trunk head)

                 known issue on trunk from test history)

    TI2: 870411 (PLAN-2596r255 GPU Core CS CSF, L64_CSF scenarios)

commit 440da291bdade9db4ecc54f3dc8eb7c782c63144
Author: Susan Su <Susan.Su@mediatek.com>
Date:   Fri Jan 12 20:07:00 2024 +0800

    [ALPS07344379] [r38p1] GPUCORE-34359: fix protected mode rotate issue
    
    [Detail]
    GPUCORE-34359: Avoid sending status update req for all non-idle groups
    This commit uses a group level flag to track if the reevaluation is
    required or not.
    
    Made an improvement to prevent the needless deprioritizing of protected
    group if more work work is submitted for a higher priority normal group
    or it is unblocked during protected mode execution.
    A flag was set so that Scheduler can reevaluate the idle status of that
    higher priority normal group and get a precise idea of whether that
    group has actually become non-idle or not by sending a STATUS_UPDATE
    request, but that resulted in Scheduler sending STATUS_UPDATE request
    for the other normal non-idle low priority groups also.
    
    ARM ticket: 00431963
    ARM ipdelivery: 4178/80d4a6a.diff
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: 047e3952a60681a1c6c083ff4dc3c77614958299
    
    CR-Id: ALPS07344379
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver
    Change-Id: I467a832c33e918946f14a8bcf8b8a65b512be7c2

commit 20ebe7682c24c2c8ef08484b1df914eaf95fa451
Author: Susan Su <Susan.Su@mediatek.com>
Date:   Fri Jan 12 20:06:56 2024 +0800

    [ALPS07344379] [r38p1] GPUCORE-34359: fix protected mode rotate issue
    
    [Detail]
    GPUCORE-34359: Avoid needless tocks on CSG idle events during normal execution
    This commit prevents the needless tocks.
    
    Improvements to ensure faster entry into the protected mode by scheduling a tock when a
    PROTM_PEND event is received after the CSG idle event.
    The change inadvertently impacted the regular case, where there is no
    execution done in protected mode, by scheduling a tock on every CSG
    idle event. The extra tocks resulted in more requests being sent to the
    FW, and thus an increase in the value of l2_ext_read_beats was observed.
    
    ARM ticket: 00431963
    ARM ipdelivery: 4176/5f79c43.diff
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: afa13d15ce36858ddd0ecea3b92f8ba35989f4cc
    
    CR-Id: ALPS07344379
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver
    Change-Id: Ib0f296717f4f5f973da4d2835c7b94e9a0ff09b3

    [ALPS07259820] fix gpu random hang issue
    
    [Root Cause]
    The issue can occur when there is more than one fragment context active
    in the GPU and the fragment work is terminated. The fragment endpoint
    does not encode the context ID correctly in the TERMINATED payload so
    any context open with a non-zero context ID value may not be detected
    as finished in the CSF.
    
    [Solution]
    ARM Ticket: 00411047
    ARM Patch: https://code.ipdelivery.arm.com/c/GPU/mali-ddk/+/4120
    
    GPUCORE-33944 Handle CS_FATAL cs_unrecoverable event
    GPUCORE-33946 CSFFW: Fragment iter disabling timeout WA
    GPUCORE-34091 Assertion happened in Firmware code when handling
                  CFG_ALLOC_EN request, 4085/3
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: a417a48a203cc8442c7cf1ef4c1aff8282ebd965
    
    Signed-off-by: GuanWen Chen <gw.chen@mediatek.com>
    CR-Id: ALPS07259820
    Feature: ARM GPU DDK driver
    Change-Id: I8317897d9a03c8ea50264a9ad9a7824efe5931ea

    [ALPS06367071] ARM:CSFFW:Update iter timeouts HALTING/PAUSING/DISABLING
    
    [Detail]
    patch 3538
    This patch updates iter timeouts for HALTING/PAUSING transitions,
    which was set to 200ms, to provide enough time for long running
    shaders that may potentially take a few seconds to complete.
    The new value is set to mimic the one in JM GPUs.
    This commit changes HALTING/PAUSING transition timeout to 5 sec
    to approximate it to hard stop timeout in JM. The DISABLING timeout,
    which is used as a WA for a HW bug in TODX and TTUX, is set to 0.1s
    and detached from the HALTING/PAUSING transition timeout one.

commit 8ce8ab9f73501ca0d0918c23c7cc33bffaa6fc78
Author: mtk15651 <bocheng.chen@mediatek.com>
Date:   Fri Jan 12 19:52:48 2024 +0800

    [ALPS06388678] GPU:Avoid using pm lock for update of User reg page mapping
    
    When a Base context is created, the User register page that houses the
    LATEST_FLUSH register is mapped to the process address space.
    This allows Userspace to directly access the LATEST_FLUSH reg value.
    As the register is not accessible once GPU is powered down, a dummy
    page is mapped before the power down.
    
    Previously kbdev->pm.lock was being used to synchronize between the
    CPU page fault handler for the User register page mapping and zapping
    of the PTE corresponding to the CPU mapping of User register page.
    This sometimes resulted in the blocking of the render thread of
    Application inside the page fault handler.
    
    This commit uses kbdev->csf.reg_lock for the synchronization, as also
    done in 55ed9ea04f05b9497b889c5616d4ac5064d0af7c, which has a much
    narrower scope and so avoids the stalling of render thread.
    
    TI2: 790459 (PLAN-11965r596 DDK Precommit, 1 build failure is unrelated)
    TI2: 790180 (BASE_L64_TODX)
    TI2: 790449 (BASE CSF tests on Android)
    TI2: 790824 (More BASE CSF tests on Android, failure for power test is
                 unrelated)
    
    MTK-Commit-Id: e38ab0e03c0c53a62d4f3e507536412dbbe62058
    
    CR-Id: ALPS06388678
    Feature: GPU DVFS
    Change-Id: I59510709651feb428d2a00c60e1b2a5222405e00
    Signed-off-by: mtk15651 <bocheng.chen@mediatek.com>

commit 9fbaefd6a04c2eaf4b1ed453ab48fc3f37a16aea
Author: mtk15651 <bocheng.chen@mediatek.com>
Date:   Fri Jan 12 19:52:48 2024 +0800

    [ALPS06388678] GPU:Improve idleness detection for active queue post idle
    
    From ARM official pztch
    
    1.GPUCORE-30827 Improve idleness detection for active queue post idle notif
    
    This commit adds extra checks in the GPU idle worker before proceeding
    with suspending all CSGs and powering off the GPU whereby CSGs could
    have become active after the firmware has issued an idle notification
    but before the host has received & processed this notification.
    
    This issue could lead to active CSGs being suspended unnecessarily. In
    addition to that, the scheduler will only re-examine those CSGs in the
    next tick event which adds further latency.
    
    Additional changes:
    - Use a dedicated workqueue for GPU idle worker to improve latency
    
    - All backward compat test failures were reported in GPUCORE-31565
    - https://ti2.gpu.arm.com/tables/suite/11819611103 Scenario failed because no branch was specified in the commit message, otherwise all tests passed
    
    TI2: 784720 (precommit)
    TI2: 784718 (GPU Core CS CSF)
    TI2: 785021 (BASE_CSF_SCHEDULER on Android platforms)
    Type: Fix
    
    2.GPUCORE-31672 Handle CSG IRQs before global IRQs
    
    There exists a race condition where multiple IRQs could arrive at the
    host at the same time e.g., either by firmwares optimisation or the
    host CPU being overloaded. In which case it is not possible for the host
    to determine which IRQ was raised first.
    
    The order in which an IRQ is raised (thus handled) is important for the
    host regarding handling of the GPU idle IRQ: if the GPU has become
    non-idle again after the GPU idle IRQ has arrived, but before the GPU
    idle worker is executed then the host needs to ignore that idle event.
    
    Currently the host always handles GPU IRQs first before CSG IRQs which
    means that in case a SYNC update and a GPU idle notification are raised
    in that order, but is handled by the host at the same time then itd
    lead to the host ignoring that idle event and incorrectly leave the GPU
    powered on.
    
    This commit swaps the order in which those IRQs are handled. In the
    worst-case scenario, the GPU would be incorrectly powered off, only to
    be powered on shortly after. This seems to be a preferable alternative
    to leaving the GPU powered on.
    
    It is expected that this order of handling IRQ shall work for most
    contents that are:
    - Running at VSync: the GPU would correctly be powered off inter-frames.
    - GPU-bound: the GPU is not expected to become idle thus this race
      condition doesnt apply.
    
    TI2: 793304 (precommit)
    TI2: 793302 (GPU Core CS CSF)
    
    3.GPUCORE-31999: Fix intermittent failure for BASE_CSF_PERFORMANCE_TESTS
    
    An improvement was made in GPUCORE-30827 to avoid the power down of GPU
    when more work was submitted & executed after the GPU idle notification
    interrupt. For that Extract offset of all the queues are sampled on GPU
    idle notification interrupt and then the sampled value are compared with
    the current values from gpu_idle_worker.
    
    That improvement resulted in an intermittent failure for the gpu sleep
    test because gpu_idle_worker wrongly inferred that GPU is not
    idle due to the change in Extract offset values and skipped the GPU
    power down.
    For the sampling loop, csg_slots_idle_mask was being used to loop
    through the idle groups and that caused the problem.
    
    A race can happen between the GPU idle notification interrupt and the
    Scheduling tick, due to which momentarily the csg_slots_idle_mask is
    cleared and so the sampling loop skips updating the Extract offset
    value for all the queues. As a result the gpu_idle_worker ended up
    using the stale value of Extract offsets and wrongly inferred that
    more work was submitted and thus skip the GPU power down.
    
    The clearing of csg_slots_idle_mask happens when Scheduler re-evaluates
    the idle status of CSGs before sending the STATUS_UPDATE requests and
    the mask is restored after the STATUS_UPDATE requests have completed
    for all the CSGs, but the scheduler.interrupt_lock is released in
    between which results in a race.
    
    This commit avoids the race problem by using the csg_inuse_bitmap for
    the sampling loop.

    TI2: 791309 (Few Base scenarios from PLAN-12467r346 TGT CS Nightly)

commit de4636cbbb18f3d02cf856956cab8f310060204e
Author: mtk15651 <bocheng.chen@mediatek.com>
Date:   Fri Jan 12 19:51:43 2024 +0800

    [ALPS06263764] GPU: Skip resuming the idle groups on GPU power up
    
    On GPU power up, Kbase tried to put all the groups on CSG slots even
    though only one group could have become non-idle (which would happen
    in case of a full screen playback). So in most GPU power cycles, Kbase
    ended up doing a suspend and resume of groups that are idle.
    
    This commit updates both backends to resume only the non-idle groups
    when GPU is powered up or when CSG slots become free. A tock will be
    scheduled to resume an off-slot idle group when the queues bound to it
    are kicked, depending upon the priority of group and availability of
    free CSG slots.
